title_en: The tiny animal that checks our water
title_ha: TODO: Hausa title by a native speaker
audience: Hausa-speaking students, teachers and anyone curious about ponds, wells and water safety
idea: Daphnia, a water flea a few millimetres long, filters algae and bacteria out of the water it lives in, and because it is so sensitive, scientists use it to test whether chemicals are harmful to life in water.

video.presenter_prompt: A cheerful young Northern Nigerian woman scientist in a lab coat and headscarf, speaking to the camera beside a glass beaker of pond water in a bright laboratory
video.script_en: Look closely at pond water and you may see tiny animals jumping. This is Daphnia, a water flea a few millimetres long. It sweeps algae and bacteria out of the water with its legs, all day long, so a pond full of Daphnia is clearer. Daphnia is also very sensitive. If a chemical harms it, the chemical may harm other life in the water too. That is why scientists around the world test new chemicals on Daphnia before they are allowed near rivers and lakes.
